chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from al-Amir ibn Ribah, from Amr ibn al-Walid, from Sa'd al-Iskaf, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Three things are back-breaking: a man who overestimates his deeds, forgets his sins, and is conceited of his own opinion.

key_terms.أَعْجَبَ بِرَأْيِهِ: being conceited of one's own opinion

ai.seo_question: What are the three things that break a person's back spiritually according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) to highlight the subtle spiritual dangers of self-deception, where overestimation of deeds and arrogance in one's own judgment lead to a 'breaking' of the soul's resilience. This triad of ailments underscores the Shia emphasis on *muraqabah* (self-monitoring) and *tawadu* (humility) as essential antidotes to the ego's inflation.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-85 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdulhamid, on the authority of Amir ibn Ribah, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Walid, on the authority of Sa’d al-Iskaf that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said, “
Three things are back- breaking: overestimating one’s deeds; forgetting one’s sins and being conceited.”
